stories.title: The Magic of Maps
stories.description: Ajay contrasts the confusion of medieval rulers like Akbar and Aurangzeb, who relied on local knowledge and 'Chinese whispers', with the clarity and 'God's eye view' provided by maps.

stories.title: George Everest and The Great Arc
stories.description: The story of the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India, started by the British (Robert Clive) and led by George Everest. It involved decades of mundane, painstaking work with theodolites to create a unified map of India, a true public good.

stories.title: Barun Mitra's Fight for Tribal Rights
stories.description: Amit tells the story of activist Barun Mitra using historical Google Earth satellite imagery to prove that tribals in Gujarat had lived on their land for decades, winning them land rights. Once they owned the land, they built toilets, showing how incentives change behavior.

stories.title: Apple vs. The Music Industry
stories.description: Ajay uses the story of how the music industry united to force Apple to abandon its proprietary DRM format for MP3s as an analogy for how tech giants are now uniting around OpenStreetMaps to prevent a Google Maps monopoly.

stories.title: Thelma & Louise in Saudi Arabia
stories.description: Amit shares an anecdote that the movie 'Thelma & Louise' would be only 4 minutes long in Saudi Arabia because all scenes of women driving were censored.

core_ideas.description: Maps are non-rival and non-excludable. The British created them as a public good, but the post-independence Indian state failed to maintain access. Technology (Google, OSM) has now democratized them again.
The Indian state lacks the capacity to maintain high-quality maps, but technology (GPS, satellite imagery) allows private actors and citizens to bypass state failure and create their own solutions.

core_ideas.item: OpenStreetMaps as a Digital Public Good
core_ideas.description: Ajay argues that OpenStreetMaps (OSM) is a true digital public good because it is open-source and community-driven, unlike Google Maps which is proprietary.
Amit argues that the democratization of the 'means of production' (media, maps) leads to a crumbling of the mainstream consensus, which is chaotic but empowering.

core_ideas.item: The Map is Not the Territory
core_ideas.description: The Borges story illustrates that a perfectly accurate map would be uselessly large and instantly outdated. Useful maps are models that abstract reality.
